title: Size‐Related Patterns of Hyperostosis in the Carangid Fish OLIGOPLITES PALOMETA (Cuvier, 1832)
content:
ABSTRACT

Hyperostosis in wild fishes remains poorly documented and quantitative information on its size-related onset and anatomical distribution in Oligoplites palometa (Cuvier, 1832) is limited. We quantified hyperostosis prevalence and described its skeletal distribution across size classes in O. palometa from two estuarine systems on the coast of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil (Guanabara Bay and Sepetiba Bay). A total of 31 specimens ranging from 45 to 510 mm TL were examined by radiography, followed by excision and morphometric analysis of the unaffected and affected bones. Hyperostosis was observed in all examined individuals ≥ 315 mm TL, whereas none was detected in specimens ≤ 82 mm. No individuals between 82 and 315 mm total length (TL) were available, limiting the assessment of the onset and progression of hyperostosis within this size range. Hyperostoses were detected in the cranium, cleithrum, dorsal pterygiophores and anal pterygiophores, with the cleithrum showing the highest prevalence (80.64%), followed by dorsal pterygiophores (77.41%), anal pterygiophores (67.7%) and cranium (61.29%). These findings indicate a consistent size-related pattern of skeletal involvement, highlighting the importance of population size structure when evaluating hyperostosis in wild fish populations.
